findings.highlight: dirty killings
findings.evidenceJa: 泥仕合みたいな殺し合い
findings.governingReading: Shirou rejects killing one another in an ugly, mire-like struggle.
findings.explanation: Dirty killings sounds like killings performed dishonorably and loses the mutual, degrading deadlock image of 泥仕合.

findings.highlight: He doesn’t even need to ask me.
findings.evidenceJa: 言われるまでもない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks he needs no one to tell him; his decision is already firm.
findings.explanation: Ask changes the passive idiom’s refusal to be instructed into commentary on Kirei’s question.

findings.highlight: I don’t care. If that’s Emiya-kun’s choice, I can’t say anything about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 構わないわ。それが衛宮くんの選択なら、わたしがどうこう言える事じゃないでしょう
findings.governingReading: Rin says she has no objection; if it is Shirou’s choice, she has no standing to interfere.
findings.explanation: I don’t care makes her sound emotionally indifferent rather than restrained by respect for his agency.

findings.highlight: Rips off my arm with his bare hands.
findings.evidenceJa: その五指を、容赦なく俺の腕にめり込ませ
findings.governingReading: Kirei mercilessly sinks all five fingers into Shirou’s arm without physically wounding it.
findings.explanation: The English activates a line claiming the arm is ripped off, directly contradicting the intact, uninjured arm described two pages later.

findings.highlight: that’s a special magi
findings.evidenceJa: 特殊な魔術師だったか
findings.governingReading: It is a special kind of magus who heals the body by repairing the spirit.
findings.explanation: A special magi combines a singular article with the plural noun and is grammatically malformed.

findings.highlight: remove the infected part
findings.evidenceJa: 腫瘍を取り除く
findings.governingReading: The reputed technique removes a tumor without putting a scalpel into the patient.
findings.explanation: Infected part replaces a tumor with infection, changing the medical condition used in Shirou’s analogy.

findings.highlight: an unusual act used in uncivilized areas
findings.evidenceJa: 未開の地で使われる外法
findings.governingReading: Spiritual treatment is a heterodox or forbidden art associated with undeveloped lands.
findings.explanation: Unusual act removes the religious and magical prohibition in 外法 and makes a practiced art sound like a one-off action.

findings.highlight: it should not matter if the kind of magic I know is unfit for a priest
findings.evidenceJa: どのような魔術を好もうと神父失格である事は変わるまい
findings.governingReading: Since practicing any Magecraft already disqualifies him as a priest, which kind he favors cannot change that status.
findings.explanation: The English makes the type of magic itself “unfit for a priest” and loses Kirei’s argument that his disqualification is invariant.

findings.highlight: there are only a few in the church that can handle spirits as well as you do
findings.evidenceJa: 教会の秘蹟使いだって、貴方ほど霊体を繕える人はごく一部
findings.governingReading: Even among the Church’s sacrament practitioners, very few can mend spiritual bodies as well as Kirei.
findings.explanation: The English removes the specialist role and weakens mending spirits into generic handling.

findings.highlight: the spirit is only a contact treatment relying on the body
findings.evidenceJa: 霊媒は肉体に依存する接触治療にすぎない
findings.governingReading: Mediumistic treatment is still only contact treatment dependent on the body.
findings.explanation: The English makes “the spirit” itself a treatment and produces a broken body tag, obscuring the contrast with touching the body-independent soul.

findings.highlight: Kirei left you a Command Spell to force her to agree
findings.evidenceJa: それを力ずくで執行する為に令呪を一つだけ残した
findings.governingReading: Kirei leaves one Command Spell to enforce cancellation if Saber refuses to recognize it.
findings.explanation: Force her to agree changes coercive execution of the contract break into compelled assent, implying her agreement is what makes it valid.

findings.highlight: break the contract with Saber by choice
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の判断だけで白紙に戻す
findings.governingReading: Shirou would erase the contract by his judgment alone.
findings.explanation: By choice omits the unilateral exclusion of Saber that makes the act feel like betrayal.

findings.highlight: My legs hurt like they’re about to tear off
findings.evidenceJa: 骨には亀裂が入って
findings.governingReading: The sweep has cracked the bones in both legs, which now hurt as though they might tear off.
findings.explanation: The English preserves extreme pain but deletes the confirmed structural injury.

findings.highlight: take that body
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=そのからだ char=4]魔力回路を貰い受ける
findings.governingReading: Saber says she will take Shirou’s Magic Circuits, displayed with “that body” as the ruby reading.
findings.explanation: The English retains only body and deletes the system term that explains what she needs from killing him.

findings.highlight: No matter how inexperienced you  are,  are as a magus
findings.evidenceJa: いかに未熟だろうと
findings.governingReading: However immature or untrained Shirou is, he still has enough power to anchor Saber.
findings.explanation: The English contains duplicated alternatives inside the active line and is grammatically broken.

findings.highlight: It would be bad for both you and me
findings.evidenceJa: 俺だけでなくセイバーさえ、取り返しのつかない事になるだろう
findings.governingReading: Both Shirou and even Saber would face consequences that could never be undone.
findings.explanation: Would be bad removes irreversibility and the emphatic extension from himself to Saber.

findings.highlight: find a new Master
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=マスター char=3]寄り代を見つける
findings.governingReading: Saber will seek a new vessel or medium, read as Master, before her body fails.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the system role and deletes the vessel concept explaining the bodily anchoring function.

findings.highlight: I pray to the Command Spell on my left hand to abolish the contract
findings.evidenceJa: 令呪に、セイバーとの契約破棄を念じていた
findings.governingReading: Shirou directs or concentrates the intention to break the contract into the Command Spell.
findings.explanation: Pray to introduces religious supplication to the mark rather than use of command-bearing intent.

findings.highlight: I didn’t even have a chance to see it, scream, nor turn and run.
findings.evidenceJa: 言葉を交わす猶予も
findings.governingReading: There is no interval even to exchange words before the attack lands.
findings.explanation: Scream replaces reciprocal speech with a unilateral panic reaction absent from the fragmented source.

findings.highlight: And they burst.
findings.evidenceJa: 爆ぜた。
findings.governingReading: Something bursts or erupts in Shirou’s fractured perception before he can identify the attack.
findings.explanation: They supplies a plural subject that most naturally points to the girl and giant, making the figures themselves burst.

findings.highlight: just the sheer force of the weapon moving  causes my arm to[line4]  takes m[line4]
findings.evidenceJa: その場に留まったまま凶器を振り上げ、その剣圧だけで
findings.governingReading: Without moving from the spot, the giant raises his weapon; its pressure alone carries away part of Shirou’s chest.
findings.explanation: The English line is truncated into incompatible fragments and introduces an arm before the later chest reveal.

findings.highlight: It flew off from my shoulder and blood is spilling out like crazy
findings.evidenceJa: どこが。根元から[line4]？
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot yet identify what flew off or whether it came away from the base.
findings.explanation: The English resolves the uncertainty as shoulder amputation and adds uncontrolled bleeding before the source reveals a missing section of chest.

findings.highlight: assisted suicide
findings.evidenceJa: カイシャク
findings.governingReading: The girl calls the finishing act kaishaku, the attendant’s beheading that ends ritual suicide, within her distorted lesson about seiza and death.
findings.explanation: Assisted suicide names the whole modern category rather than the specific coup de grâce and breaks the Japanese cultural mechanism of her joke.

findings.highlight: One of my lungs has been blown about fifty meters behind me.
findings.evidenceJa: 胸の片方、穴が開いて俺の後ろに吹き飛んでいる
findings.governingReading: One side of Shirou’s chest has been blown away behind him, leaving a hole.
findings.explanation: The English specifies a lung and adds fifty meters, neither of which is stated in the source.

findings.highlight: Things that used to be my legs and meat and bones are beautifully turned into two-dimensional objects.
findings.evidenceJa: 体の下が二次元になってしまって、見ても信じられない程に平たくなった
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s lower body has become two-dimensional in metaphor, flattened beyond belief by press-like weapon pressure.
findings.explanation: The English inserts “beautifully,” itemizes flesh and bones, duplicates alternatives, and changes one flattened lower body into plural objects.

findings.highlight: My senses freeze.
findings.evidenceJa: 理性が凍結する。
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s rational faculty freezes after the girl destroys his last hope.
findings.explanation: Senses changes higher reasoning into sensory perception, despite his continuing ability to feel and hear.

findings.highlight: My senses will not die no matter how much I am hurt.
findings.evidenceJa: どれほど傷つけられても意識は死んでくれない。
findings.governingReading: No degree of injury will allow Shirou’s consciousness to die or disappear.
findings.explanation: Senses narrows the magically sustained consciousness that makes the torture possible.

findings.highlight: Emiya Shirou gives up all hope.
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=きぼう char=2]思考を持つ事を放棄した
findings.governingReading: The ending says Shirou abandons possessing thought, while ruby reads that thought as hope.
findings.explanation: The English retains only hope and deletes the visible act of relinquishing thought that connects to frozen rationality.
